title: Burkina Faso Severs Diplomatic Relations with France (June 26, 2026)
detail:
Burkina Faso's military government, led by Capt. Ibrahim Traoré, announced on Friday, June 26, 2026 that it was severing diplomatic relations with France effective immediately — its former colonial ruler and, until the 2022 coups, its principal security partner. The junta's statement accused Paris of 'blatant neo-colonial ambitions and active support for subversive networks and terrorists,' without providing public evidence.

France's Foreign Ministry spokesman Pascal Confavreux said Paris 'regrets the hostile and unfounded decision, which illustrates the worrying drift of the Burkinabè authorities,' adding that 'necessary reciprocal measures are currently under review.'

The rupture is the culmination of a multi-year unwinding of French influence across the AES bloc: Burkina Faso expelled French troops in 2023, ejected French diplomats in April 2024 over alleged 'subversive activities,' and has increasingly aligned with Russia (Africa Corps), Turkey, and China for military and economic partnerships. Mali and Niger — the other two AES juntas — had already downgraded or severed comparable ties with Paris in prior years. The move leaves France with no formal diplomatic channel in any of the three central Sahel states.
